subject.title: fix(exec): stop isolated state dirs from moving live approvals

question: Should bare `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` relocation remain a supported approval-policy upgrade path, or should every custom state root become independent even when an older default-state policy exists?
rationale: The branch deliberately removes a shipped migration and fail-closed coupling at an exec-approval boundary, so code inspection cannot decide whether compatibility or strict trust-scope isolation is the intended product contract.

options.title: Isolate with explicit import
options.body: Remove automatic cross-state mutation, add an operator-confirmed source-to-target import or copy flow, and keep first use safe until the custom policy is configured.

options.title: Accept full isolation
options.body: Land independent scopes as written, with clear upgrade communication that existing custom-state users must configure a new policy before running commands.

options.title: Preserve relocation migration
options.body: Keep direct doctor migration for bare state relocation while continuing to block named-profile, automated, update, watch, and macOS implicit cross-scope imports.

recommendation.title: Isolate with explicit import
recommendation.body: Remove automatic cross-state mutation, add an operator-confirmed source-to-target import or copy flow, and keep first use safe until the custom policy is configured.

likelyOwner.reason: The same person introduced the current direct-doctor capability and owns the present cross-platform follow-up, making them the strongest history-backed decision owner.
